threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground' and get baffled by the number of buses that don’t even stop at the station.
Last week on the 50, a bloke serenaded the whole bus with old soul tunes. We got a free gig while dodging the usual late-night chaos.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The way the Kottbusser Tor U-Bahn station smells of curry and sweat on a summer afternoon—then echoes of laughter spill from the Späti next door.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Friedrichshain, the U-Bahn literally stops for traffic lights. Only here will you see a train waiting while cars zoom past.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by how they instinctively navigate through the busker chaos on Valencia—no slowing down, just a casual pivot.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy feeding pizza to the pigeons at Civic Center while waiting for the bus. Muni delays turn into moments of urban wildlife watching.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all we do is party in the plazas, but most nights you'll find locals tucked into the corner of a bar, chatting over a vermut. It's the quiet moments that matter.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still ask for tap water at restaurants; locals just order a 'vino' or the house specialty.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still ask for directions to the nearest 'tube station' instead of just saying 'the overground.'
Heard a couple arguing on the 196 last night; she said he liked the taste of her tears. Talk about dramatic fare dodging.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Last week, I saw three generations of a family sharing shawarma on the curb, while a street musician played a haunting tune. That's when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Kreuzberg's hidden beer gardens have a surprising mix of local brews and international street food, perfect for lazy summer afternoons.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their ability to dodge a pigeon while simultaneously balancing a burrito and scrolling through their phone.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the Muni stuck at Civic Center yesterday because a dog decided to take a nap on the tracks. Only in SF, right?

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all Gràcia's plazas are for tourists. Locals know the best conversations happen in the small alleys over a pint.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a new face by their unwavering enthusiasm for the 'Flamenc' show at the corner bar—like they haven’t seen the one-man guitar gig before.
